1	# ArtAgents
2	
3	![ArtAgents architecture: orchestrators route work to executors and render elements](docs/assets/artagents-orchestration.png)
4	
5	ArtAgents is a file-based toolkit for producing Reigh-compatible video edits,
6	event-talk renders, generative timelines, and image/video assets.
7	
8	The public model has three canonical concepts:
9	
10	- **Orchestrators** coordinate workflows.
11	- **Executors** run concrete work.
12	- **Elements** are render/custom building blocks such as effects, animations, and transitions.
13	
14	Use canonical commands for new work.
15	
16	`python3 -m artagents` is the executable package gateway and single command gateway.
17	Use it to discover, inspect, validate, install, and run every
18	orchestrator, executor, and element. `python3 pipeline.py` remains a
19	compatibility launcher, and the `bin/*.py` scripts are thin direct launchers for
20	specialized/manual use.
21	
22	## Agent Prompt
23	
24	Copy this into a coding agent:
25	
26	```text
27	Use the ArtAgents repo:
28	https://github.com/banodoco/ArtAgents
29	
30	First read AGENTS.md, README.md, and SKILL.md, then run:
31	git status --short
32	python3 pipeline.py doctor
33	
34	Use canonical terms and commands: orchestrators, executors, and elements.
35	
36	Keep generated files under runs/ unless the task explicitly touches generated
37	Remotion registries. Do not commit secrets or media. Before editing, check for
38	dirty user files and do not overwrite unrelated changes.
39	```
40	
41	## First Commands
42	
43	Run these from the repository root before making changes:
44	
45	```bash
46	python3 pipeline.py --help
47	python3 -m artagents --help
48	git status --short
49	python3 pipeline.py doctor
50	python3 pipeline.py orchestrators list
51	python3 pipeline.py executors list
52	python3 pipeline.py elements list
53	python3 pipeline.py setup
54	```
55	
56	`setup` is dry-run by default. It reports the managed default element sync and
57	local dependency-install plan without mutating the workspace. Use
58	`python3 pipeline.py setup --apply` only when you intend to materialize defaults
59	and run local element install helpers.
60	
61	## Quick Start
62	
63	```bash
64	# Source-video hype cut
65	python3 pipeline.py --video source.mp4 --brief brief.txt --out runs/example --render
66	
67	# Audio-backed timeline
68	python3 pipeline.py --audio rant.wav --brief brief.txt --out runs/audio --render
69	
70	# Pure-generative timeline
71	python3 pipeline.py --brief brief.txt --theme 2rp --out runs/generative --render --target-duration 28
72	
73	# Pure-generative sample brief
74	python3 pipeline.py --brief examples/briefs/cinematic.txt --out runs/cinematic --render --target-duration 15
75	
76	# Event-talk render
77	python3 bin/event_talks.py render --manifest runs/event/talks.json --out-dir runs/event/rendered
78	```
79	
80	Generated outputs belong under `runs/`. That directory is ignored by git and can
81	contain frames, JSON files, audits, and rendered videos from local experiments.
82	
83	## Discovery
84	
85	```bash
86	python3 pipeline.py orchestrators list
87	python3 pipeline.py orchestrators inspect builtin.hype --json
88	python3 pipeline.py executors list
89	python3 pipeline.py executors inspect builtin.render --json
90	python3 pipeline.py elements list
91	python3 pipeline.py elements inspect effects text-card --json
92	```
93	
94	Use these JSON commands as the runtime index for agents. The registry output
95	includes each folder-backed orchestrator or executor root and its `skill_file`,
96	so agents should load only the entrypoint repo skill plus the specific
97	folder-level `SKILL.md` needed for the task. Do not merge every executor and
98	orchestrator skill into one large runtime prompt.
99	
100	Runnable implementations have exactly one public folder format:
101	`artagents/orchestrators/<slug>/{orchestrator.yaml,SKILL.md,run.py}` for
102	orchestrators and `artagents/executors/<slug>/{executor.yaml,SKILL.md,run.py}`
103	for executors, with optional local `src/` modules. Top-level `artagents/*.py`
104	files are shared libraries or system commands, not alternate runnable
105	implementations.
106	
107	When ArtAgents is missing a reusable capability, use `docs/creating-tools.md`
108	before adding files. Create an executor for one concrete unit of work, an
109	orchestrator for a workflow, and an element for a reusable render building
110	block. Copy from `docs/templates/executor/`, `docs/templates/orchestrator/`, or
111	`docs/templates/element/` so new public tools keep the expected shape.
112	
113	Default orchestrators include `builtin.hype`, `builtin.event_talks`,
114	`builtin.thumbnail_maker`, and `builtin.understand`. Default executors include the built-in pipeline
115	stages such as `builtin.transcribe`, `builtin.cut`, `builtin.render`, and
116	`builtin.validate`, plus external executors such as `external.moirae` and
117	`external.vibecomfy.run`. VibeComfy is an executor only,
118	not an orchestrator.
119	
120	Default elements are bundled in this repository and can be synced into
121	`.artagents/elements/managed`. User-editable forks and overrides live under
122	`.artagents/elements/overrides`:
123	
124	```bash
125	python3 pipeline.py elements sync --dry-run
126	python3 pipeline.py elements fork effects text-card
127	python3 pipeline.py elements install effects text-card
128	python3 pipeline.py elements update --dry-run
129	```
130	
131	Element source priority is active theme, then `.artagents/elements/overrides`,
132	then `.artagents/elements/managed`, then bundled defaults in
133	`artagents/elements/bundled`.
134	
135	## Main Commands
136	
137	```bash
138	# Rerun a pipeline from a specific stage
139	python3 pipeline.py --video source.mp4 --brief brief.txt --out runs/example --from cut --render
140	
141	# Audit a run
142	python3 pipeline.py audit --run runs/example
143	python3 pipeline.py audit --run runs/example --json
144	
145	# Fetch canonical Reigh data through the app Edge Function
146	python3 pipeline.py reigh-data --project-id <PROJECT_UUID> --shot-id <SHOT_UUID> --out runs/reigh/shot.json
147	
148	# Render a Reigh-compatible timeline/assets pair
149	python3 bin/render_remotion.py \
150	  --timeline runs/example/briefs/my-brief/hype.timeline.json \
151	  --assets runs/example/briefs/my-brief/hype.assets.json \
152	  --out runs/example/briefs/my-brief/render.mp4
153	```
154	
155	## Repo Map
156	
157	```text
158	artagents/                 Python implementation
159	artagents/orchestrators/   Canonical orchestrator folders, registry, runner, and CLI
160	artagents/executors/       Canonical executor folders, registry, runner, and CLI
161	artagents/elements/        Element schema, registry, CLI, and bundled defaults
162	.artagents/elements/       Local managed defaults and user overrides
163	bin/                       Direct launchers backed by canonical executor and orchestrator folders
164	agents/                    Agent configuration
165	remotion/                  Remotion renderer project
166	scripts/                   Development and code-generation scripts
167	docs/                      Architecture notes, creation guide, and templates
168	examples/                  Schema fixtures and committed sample briefs under examples/briefs/
169	_reference/                Copied Reigh contract references
170	runs/                      Ignored local outputs
171	```
172	
173	`python3 -m artagents` is the package entry point. `pipeline.py` remains a
174	compatibility launcher, and `bin/*.py` launchers call the matching canonical
175	executor or orchestrator modules when you need a single stage directly.
176	`python3 pipeline.py doctor` also validates the canonical repo structure: public
177	executor folders must contain `executor.yaml`, `run.py`, and `SKILL.md`; public
178	orchestrator folders must contain `orchestrator.yaml`, `run.py`, and `SKILL.md`;
179	legacy public packages such as conductor/performer folders are rejected.
180	
181	## Outputs
182	
183	The main pipeline writes source-level artifacts into the run directory and
184	brief-level artifacts under `briefs/<slug>/`:
185	
186	```text
187	runs/example/
188	  transcript.json
189	  scenes.json
190	  shots.json
191	  pool.json
192	  audit/
193	  briefs/
194	    my-brief/
195	      arrangement.json
196	      hype.timeline.json
197	      hype.assets.json
198	      hype.metadata.json
199	      hype.mp4
200	      validation.json
201	```
202	
203	## Generated Files
204	
205	Normal generated media, frames, intermediate JSON, and local reports belong
206	under `runs/` or another ignored output directory. Do not commit secrets, large
207	source media, rendered videos, or local dependency environments.
208	
209	Generated Remotion registry files are source artifacts when element code
210	changes. Keep generated siblings synchronized across `.ts`, `.js`, `.d.ts`, and
211	`.map` outputs in `remotion/src`, and scan for stale element aliases after
212	regeneration:
213	
214	```bash
215	python3 scripts/gen_effect_registry.py
216	rg "@workspace-|workspace-effects|workspace-animations|workspace-transitions" remotion/src scripts remotion -n
217	```
218	
219	## Development
220	
221	```bash
222	python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
223	pytest
224	
225	cd remotion
226	npm run typecheck
227	npm run smoke
228	npm run gen-types
229	```
230	
231	Run `npm run gen-types` after effect, animation, transition, or theme element
232	changes. Local secrets belong in `.env`, `.env.*`, or `this.env`; these are
233	ignored by git.
234	
235	## Dirty-File Caution
236	
237	Always inspect `git status --short` before editing. This repository often has
238	active generated artifacts and local skill edits. In particular, do not overwrite
239	unrelated changes in curated executor skill files such as
240	`artagents/executors/moirae/SKILL.md` or
241	`artagents/executors/vibecomfy/SKILL.md`.
242	
243	## License

245	Open Source Native License (OSNL) v0.2. See `LICENSE` for the full terms.

You're right — I just audited my draft against the original and the instructions got worse, not just decorated. Specific failures:

- **INSCRIBE** suggests writing *to* AGENTS.md/README.md/SKILL.md. The original says *read* them. Wrong verb.
- **TRUE NAMES** lists the three concepts but drops the actual instruction ("use these terms in commands and discussion").

- **DIVINE** loses the ordering signal ("first read, *then* run").
- "Conjurings", "vessel" — agent will probably figure it out, but a human glancing at the README to copy this loses confidence that it's still a real prompt.

The fix is to keep the visual language (border, knotwork, centered cartouches, spaced caps) but make the verbs do real work. The art comes from the layout, not from obfuscated vocabulary. Revised verse set:

> AGENT

Yes — and that's a much better idea. Reasons:

1. **Self-demonstrating.** The spell's whole point is "everything passes through `python3 -m artagents` and orchestrators conduct workflows." Right now the first rite *contradicts* that by hand-rolling a multi-step shell recipe. If it's an orchestrator, the rite becomes a one-liner that *is* an example of the thing being taught.
2. **Cleaner spell.** The boxed prompt + multi-line `generate_image` invocation can collapse to:
   ```
   python3 -m artagents orchestrators run builtin.first_rite
   ```
   The funny Saint Peter prompt moves into the orchestrator's `SKILL.md` / `run.py` where it belongs.
3. **Future-proof.** If you ever change how images get generated (swap to vibecomfy, add an open step, etc.), the spell doesn't need to change.

Shape: a `builtin.first_rite` orchestrator that (a) writes the patron-saint prompt to `runs/first-rite/prompt.txt`, (b) calls `builtin.generate_image`, (c) opens the result. Probably built from the `docs/templates/orchestrator/` template — which means the rite *itself* also demonstrates FORGE.

Two small calls before I build it:

1. **Name** — `builtin.first_rite`, `builtin.greet`, `builtin.hello`, or something else? `first_rite` keeps the spell's vocabulary; `greet` reads more like a conventional "hello world."
2. **Scope** — keep it locked to the Saint Peter prompt (funny, fixed, on-brand for the spell), or take an optional `--prompt` so it doubles as a generic image-gen orchestrator? I'd vote locked — a generic image-gen orchestrator is just `builtin.generate_image` with extra steps; the value of `first_rite` is being a specific, delightful onboarding moment.

121	def _parse_size(size: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
122	    match = re.fullmatch(r"([1-9][0-9]*)x([1-9][0-9]*)", size)
123	    if not match:
124	        return None
125	    return int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2))

128	def _validate_size(size: str, model: str) -> None:
129	    if size == "auto":
130	        return
131	    if model != "gpt-image-2":
132	        if size not in {"1024x1024", "1536x1024", "1024x1536"}:
133	            _die("For models before gpt-image-2, size must be 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, or auto.")
134	        return
135	    parsed = _parse_size(size)
136	    if parsed is None:
137	        _die("size must be auto or WIDTHxHEIGHT, for example 1024x1024")
138	    width, height = parsed
139	    if width % 16 or height % 16:
140	        _die("gpt-image-2 size width and height must be multiples of 16px")
141	    if max(width, height) > GPT_IMAGE_2_MAX_EDGE:
142	        _die("gpt-image-2 size maximum edge length is 3840px")
143	    if max(width, height) / min(width, height) > GPT_IMAGE_2_MAX_RATIO:
144	        _die("gpt-image-2 size long edge to short edge ratio must not exceed 3:1")
145	    pixels = width * height
146	    if pixels < GPT_IMAGE_2_MIN_PIXELS or pixels > GPT_IMAGE_2_MAX_PIXELS:
147	        _die("gpt-image-2 size total pixels must be between 655,360 and 8,294,400")

154	    n = int(payload["n"])
155	    if n < 1 or n > 10:

157	    _validate_size(str(payload["size"]), model)
158	    if payload["quality"] not in QUALITIES:
159	        _die("--quality must be low, medium, high, or auto")
160	    if payload.get("background") and payload["background"] not in BACKGROUNDS:
161	        _die("--background must be opaque, auto, or transparent")
162	    if model == "gpt-image-2" and payload.get("background") == "transparent":
163	        _die("gpt-image-2 does not support transparent backgrounds; use opaque/auto or explicitly choose an older supported model")
164	    if payload.get("moderation") and payload["moderation"] not in MODERATION:
165	        _die("--moderation must be auto or low")
166	    compression = payload.get("output_compression")
167	    if compression is not None and not (0 <= int(compression) <= 100):
168	        _die("--output-compression must be between 0 and 100")

171	def _normalize_job(item: Any, index: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
172	    if isinstance(item, str):
173	        prompt = item.strip()
174	        if not prompt:
175	            _die(f"Empty prompt at item {index}")
176	        return {"prompt": prompt}
177	    if isinstance(item, dict) and str(item.get("prompt", "")).strip():
178	        return dict(item)

180	    return {}

183	def _load_prompts(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
184	    if not path.is_file():
185	        _die(f"Prompts file not found: {path}")
186	    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
187	    if not text:
188	        _die(f"Prompts file is empty: {path}")
189	    if path.suffix.lower() == ".json":
190	        data = json.loads(text)
191	        if not isinstance(data, list):
192	            _die("JSON prompts file must contain an array")
193	        return [_normalize_job(item, index + 1) for index, item in enumerate(data)]
194	    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
195	    for line_no, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
196	        line = raw.strip()
197	        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
198	            continue
199	        if line.startswith("{") or line.startswith('"'):
200	            jobs.append(_normalize_job(json.loads(line), line_no))
201	        else:
202	            jobs.append({"prompt": line})
203	    if not jobs:
204	        _die("No prompts found")
205	    return jobs

208	def _slugify(text: str) -> str:
209	    value = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9]+", "-", text.strip().lower()).strip("-")
210	    return value[:64] or "image"

213	def _output_paths(out_dir: Path, prompt: str, fmt: str, job_index: int, n: int, explicit_out: str | None) -> list[Path]:
214	    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
215	    ext = "." + fmt
216	    if explicit_out:
217	        base = Path(explicit_out)
218	        if not base.suffix:
219	            base = base.with_suffix(ext)
220	        base = out_dir / base.name
221	    else:
222	        base = out_dir / f"{job_index:03d}-{_slugify(prompt)}{ext}"
223	    if n == 1:
224	        return [base]
225	    return [base.with_name(f"{base.stem}-{i}{base.suffix}") for i in range(1, n + 1)]

228	def _call_image_api(payload: dict[str, Any], api_key: str, timeout: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
229	    request = Request(
230	        API_URL,
231	        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),

233	        method="POST",

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Onboarding rite: summon a portrait of the maker and open it.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom artagents.executors.generate_image.run import main as generate_image_main\n\n\nPROMPT = (\n    \"An illuminated medieval manuscript page depicting Saint Peter of Banodoco, \"\n    \"patron of file-based pipelines, haloed in glowing unix prompts, quill in \"\n    \"hand inscribing ffmpeg incantations. Tiny familiar spirits labelled REIGH, \"\n    \"LOTA, and MOIRAE peer over his shoulders. Gold leaf, vellum, Celtic \"\n    \"knotwork border.\"\n)\n\n\ndef build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Run the first rite.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--out\", type=Path, default=Path(\"runs/first-rite\"))\n    parser.add_argument(\"--no-open\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"Skip opening the rendered image.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--dry-run\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"Print the plan without calling the API.\")\n    return parser\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)\n    out_dir = args.out\n    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    prompt_file = out_dir / \"prompt.txt\"\n    prompt_file.write_text(PROMPT + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    print(f\"Wrote {prompt_file}\")\n\n    images_dir = out_dir / \"images\"\n    manifest = out_dir / \"manifest.json\"\n    gen_argv = [\n        \"--prompts-file\", str(prompt_file),\n        \"--out-dir\", str(images_dir),\n        \"--manifest\", str(manifest),\n        \"--force\",\n    ]\n    if args.dry_run:\n        gen_argv.append(\"--dry-run\")\n\n    rc = generate_image_main(gen_argv)\n    if rc != 0:\n        return rc\n\n    if args.dry_run or args.no_open:\n        return 0\n\n    rendered = sorted(images_dir.glob(\"*.png\")) + sorted(images_dir.glob(\"*.jpeg\")) + sorted(images_dir.glob(\"*.webp\"))\n    if not rendered:\n        print(\"No image was rendered; nothing to open.\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 0\n\n    target = rendered[0]\n    print(f\"Opening {target}\")\n    subprocess.run([\"open\", str(target)], check=False)\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"

46	class OrchestratorRegistryError(OrchestratorValidationError):
47	    """Raised when an orchestrator registry is inconsistent."""
48	
49	
50	class OrchestratorRegistry:
51	    """Small in-memory registry keyed by orchestrator id."""
52	
53	    def __init__(
54	        self,
55	        orchestrators: Iterable[OrchestratorDefinition | dict[str, Any]] = (),
56	        *,
57	        executor_registry: ExecutorRegistry | None = None,
58	    ) -> None:
59	        self._orchestrators: dict[str, OrchestratorDefinition] = {}
60	        self._executor_registry = executor_registry
61	        for orchestrator in orchestrators:
62	            self.register(orchestrator)
63	
64	    def register(self, orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition | dict[str, Any]) -> OrchestratorDefinition:
65	        definition = validate_orchestrator_definition(orchestrator)
66	        if definition.id in self._orchestrators:
67	            raise OrchestratorRegistryError(f"duplicate orchestrator id {definition.id!r}")
68	        self._orchestrators[definition.id] = definition
69	        return definition
70	
71	    def get(self, orchestrator_id: str) -> OrchestratorDefinition:
72	        try:
73	            return self._orchestrators[orchestrator_id]
74	        except KeyError as exc:
75	            raise KeyError(f"unknown orchestrator id {orchestrator_id!r}") from exc
76	
77	    def list(self, kind: str | None = None) -> tuple[OrchestratorDefinition, ...]:
78	        if kind is not None and kind not in {"built_in", "external"}:
79	            raise OrchestratorRegistryError("kind must be one of ['built_in', 'external']")
80	        orchestrators: Iterable[OrchestratorDefinition] = self._orchestrators.values()
81	        if kind is not None:
82	            orchestrators = [orchestrator for orchestrator in orchestrators if orchestrator.kind == kind]
83	        return tuple(sorted(orchestrators, key=lambda orchestrator: orchestrator.id))
84	
85	    def validate_all(
86	        self,
87	        *,
88	        executor_registry: ExecutorRegistry | None = None,
89	    ) -> tuple[OrchestratorDefinition, ...]:
90	        for orchestrator in self._orchestrators.values():
91	            validate_orchestrator_definition(orchestrator)
92	        self._validate_child_executors(executor_registry=executor_registry)
93	        self._validate_child_orchestrators()
94	        return self.list()
95	
96	    def to_dict(self, kind: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
97	        return {"orchestrators": [orchestrator.to_dict() for orchestrator in self.list(kind=kind)]}
98	
99	    def to_json(self, *, kind: str | None = None, indent: int | None = 2) -> str:
100	        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(kind=kind), indent=indent, sort_keys=True)
101	
102	    def as_mapping(self) -> MappingProxyType[str, OrchestratorDefinition]:
103	        return MappingProxyType(dict(self._orchestrators))
104	
105	    def _validate_child_executors(self, *, executor_registry: ExecutorRegistry | None) -> None:
106	        registry = executor_registry or self._executor_registry or load_default_executor_registry()
107	        known_executor_ids = set(registry.as_mapping())
108	        for orchestrator in self._orchestrators.values():
109	            for child_executor in orchestrator.child_executors:
110	                if child_executor not in known_executor_ids:
111	                    raise OrchestratorRegistryError(
112	                        f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} references unknown child executor {child_executor!r}"
113	                    )
114	
115	    def _validate_child_orchestrators(self) -> None:
116	        known_orchestrator_ids = set(self._orchestrators)
117	        graph: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
118	        for orchestrator in self._orchestrators.values():
119	            children: list[str] = []
120	            for child_orchestrator in orchestrator.child_orchestrators:
121	                if child_orchestrator not in known_orchestrator_ids:
122	                    raise OrchestratorRegistryError(
123	                        f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} references unknown child orchestrator {child_orchestrator!r}"
124	                    )
125	                if child_orchestrator == orchestrator.id:
126	                    raise OrchestratorRegistryError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} cannot reference itself")
127	                children.append(child_orchestrator)
128	            graph[orchestrator.id] = tuple(children)
129	        self._validate_no_cycles(graph)
130	
131	    def _validate_no_cycles(self, graph: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]) -> None:
132	        visiting: set[str] = set()
133	        visited: set[str] = set()
134	        stack: list[str] = []
135	
136	        def visit(orchestrator_id: str) -> None:
137	            if orchestrator_id in visited:
138	                return
139	            if orchestrator_id in visiting:
140	                cycle = stack[stack.index(orchestrator_id) :] + [orchestrator_id]
141	                raise OrchestratorRegistryError(f"orchestrator cycle detected: {' -> '.join(cycle)}")
142	            visiting.add(orchestrator_id)
143	            stack.append(orchestrator_id)
144	            for child in graph.get(orchestrator_id, ()):
145	                visit(child)
146	            stack.pop()
147	            visiting.remove(orchestrator_id)
148	            visited.add(orchestrator_id)
149	
150	        for orchestrator_id in sorted(graph):
151	            visit(orchestrator_id)

Right — the "block-centered" trick I used for alignment makes those rows look left-leaning even though the block itself is centered. Adding bookends fixes it two ways: each prose line gets symmetric ornaments so it visually centers, and each multi-line block gets vertical "rails" so the whole block reads as a deliberate centered unit even when text inside is left-aligned.

ornaments, centered.\"\"\"\n    body = f\"{ornament}  {text}  {ornament}\"\n    return center(body)\n\ndef card(rows, ornament=\"·\"):\n    \"\"\"Block of rows framed by bookend rails at fixed \"┓\")\nparts.append(empty())\nparts.append(knot(\"╲\", \"╱\"))\nparts.append(knot(\"╱\", \"╲\"))\nparts.append(empty())\nparts.append(center(\"T H E   A R T A G E N T S   R I T No — that's a real gap. The spell currently tells the agent how to *list* all orchestrators/executors/elements but not how to drill into one and run it. To actually run `builtin.render`, an agent has to know that `executors inspect <id>` shows the inputs/outputs and `executors run <id> -- <args>` invokes it. Right now they'd have to guess or read the README.

Easy fix — add a small verse between SEE WHAT EXISTS and FORGE. Two shapes to choose from:

**Option A — minimal, just the two commands:**

```
──  ◇  R U N   O N E  ◇  ──

·  inspect first   python3 -m artagents executors inspect <id>   ·
·  then run        python3 -m artagents executors run <id> -- …  ·
```

**Option B — covers orchestrators too (same shape):**

```
──  ◇  R U N   O N E  ◇  ──

·  inspect    python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators] inspect <id>  ·
·  run        python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators] run <id> -- … ·
```

> DEVELOPER

And should the spell itself actually be central-lined within a space it has or is that not possible to do reliably?

> AGENT

Yes, reliably on GitHub — wrap the code block in a `<div align="center">`. GitHub's markdown renderer respects HTML inside markdown, and an `align="center"` on the wrapping div will center the code block (which collapses to its content width). Looks like this:

```markdown
<div align="center">

```text
[spell]
```

</div>
```

On GitHub the spell becomes a centered "card" instead of a left-aligned full-width block. Trade-offs to know:

1. **Renderer-dependent.** Works on GitHub, GitLab, most modern preview tools. Plain-text or strict CommonMark viewers will leak the `<div>` tag as visible text. For a project README on GitHub, this is fine.
2. **Doesn't affect the agent.** When someone copies the spell into a Claude/Codex/etc. prompt, the agent receives plain text — centering is purely a human-reader visual.
3. **Code-block styling may shift slightly.** Some themes render code blocks with background color filling the full width; inside the center wrapper, the background only fills the content width. On GitHub this looks intentional, like a card.

left))\n\ndef hug(text, ornament=\"·\"):\n    body = f\"{ornament}  {text}  {ornament}\"\n    return center(body)\n\ndef knot(c1, c2):\n    end = (c1 + c2) * 4\n    rail = \"─\" * 52\n    pat = end + \"╳\" + rail + \"╳\" + end\n    margin = (W - 70) // 2\n    return line(\" \" * margin + pat + \" \" * (W - margin - 70))\n\n# Block letters for ARTAGENTS (3 rows tall, 3 chars wide each)\nGLYPHS = {\n    \"A\": [\"▄▀▄\", \"█▀█\", \"▀ ▀\"],\n    \"R\": [\"█▀▄\", \"█▀▄\", \"▀ ▀\"],\n    \"T\": [\"▀█▀\", \" █ \", \" ▀ \"],\n    \"G\": [\"▄▀▀\", \"█▄█\", \"▀▀▀\"],\n    \"E\": [\"█▀▀\", \"█▀▀\", \"▀▀▀\"],\n    \"N\": [\"█▄█\", \"█ █\", \"▀ ▀\"],\n    \"S\": [\"▄▀▀\", \"▀▀▄\", \"▀▀▀\"],\n}\n\ndef block_title(word, gap=\" \"):\n    rows = [\"\", \"\", \"\"]\n    for i, ch in enumerate(word):\n        glyph = GLYPHS[ch]\n        for r in range(3):\n            rows[r] += glyph[r]\n            if i < len(word) - 1:\n                rows[r] += gap\n    return [center(r) for r in rows]\n\n\nprint(\"OPTION A — block letters (3-row title inside banner, banner becomes 5 rows tall):\")\nprint()\nprint(\"┏\" + \"━\" * W + \"┓\")\nprint(empty())\nprint(knot(\"╲\", \"╱\"))\nprint(empty())\nfor row in block_title(\"ARTAGENTS\"):\n    print(row)\nprint(empty())\nprint(knot(\"╱\", \"╲\"))\nprint(empty())\nprint()\nprint()\nprint(\"OPTION B — heavy ornament emphasis (1-row title, banner stays 3 rows):\")\nprint()\nprint(\"┏\" + \"━\" * W + \"┓\")\nprint(empty())\nprint(knot(\"╲\", \"╱\"))\nprint(center(\"═══  A R T A G E N T S  ═══\"))\nprint(knot(\"╱\", \"╲\"))\nprint(empty())\nprint()\nprint()\nprint(\"OPTION C — current 1-row title with dot bookends (no change to size, just for comparison):\")\nprint()\nprint(\"┏\" + \"━\" * W + \"┓\")\nprint(empty())\nprint(knot(\"╲\", \"╱\"))\nprint(hug(\"A R T A G E N T S\"))\nprint(knot(\"╱\", \"╲\"))\nprint(empty())\n"

1	---
2	name: "artagents"
3	description: "Use for the ArtAgents repo: file-based hype-cut/video pipeline work, source analysis, transcript/event-talk splitting, pure-generative Remotion timelines, Reigh-compatible timeline/assets JSON, validation/review loops, and GPT Image asset generation via generate_image.py."
4	---
5	
6	# ArtAgents
7	
8	ArtAgents is a file-based toolkit for producing Reigh-compatible video edits and generative timelines. Use repo-local CLIs from the repository root. `python3 -m artagents` is the executable package gateway for normal work; Use `python3 -m artagents orchestrators ...`, `python3 -m artagents executors ...`, and `python3 -m artagents elements ...` for discoverable tools. Direct launchers live under `bin/` for specialized/manual use and call canonical executor or orchestrator folder entrypoints.
9	
10	## First Checks
11	
12	Run these before editing:
13	
14	```bash
15	git status --short
16	python3 -m artagents doctor
17	python3 -m artagents orchestrators list
18	python3 -m artagents executors list
19	python3 -m artagents elements list
20	```
21	
22	Do not overwrite unrelated local changes. In particular, preserve local edits in curated executor skill files such as `artagents/executors/moirae/SKILL.md` and `artagents/executors/vibecomfy/SKILL.md` unless the user explicitly asks to edit them. Large source media and generated artifacts should stay out of git under `runs/` or another ignored output directory.
23	
24	## Upstream Friction
25	
26	When a workflow is awkward, brittle, undocumented, or requires a local workaround, tell the user directly. Suggest the smallest durable fix and, when the issue belongs in an original upstream repository rather than ArtAgents, recommend creating a PR there with the concrete file or behavior to change.
27	
28	## Core Workflows
29	
30	Source video hype cut:
31	
32	```bash
33	python3 -m artagents --video SRC.mp4 --brief brief.txt --out runs/<name> --render
34	```
35	
36	Audio-only or pure-generative timeline:
37	
38	```bash
39	python3 -m artagents --audio rant.wav --brief brief.txt --out runs/<name> --render
40	python3 -m artagents --brief brief.txt --theme <theme-id> --out runs/<name> --render --target-duration 28
41	```
42	
43	Event talk splitting:
44	
45	```bash
46	python3 bin/transcribe.py --audio talk.wav --out runs/event/transcript --env-file /path/to/.env
47	python3 bin/event_talks.py ados-sunday-template --out runs/event/talks.json
48	python3 bin/event_talks.py search-transcript --transcript runs/event/transcript/transcript.json
49	python3 bin/event_talks.py render --manifest runs/event/talks.json --out-dir runs/event/rendered
50	```
51	
52	ArtAgents has three canonical public concepts: orchestrators, executors, and elements. Orchestrators coordinate workflows. Executors run concrete work such as rendering, external tools, understanding actions, and uploading to YouTube. Elements are user-editable render building blocks such as effects, animations, and transitions.
53	
54	Entry point rule: start with `python3 -m artagents --help`, then use
55	`python3 -m artagents orchestrators ...`,
56	`python3 -m artagents executors ...`, or
57	`python3 -m artagents elements ...`. Use `bin/*.py` only when a workflow section
58	explicitly calls for a direct launcher.
59	
60	Runnable implementations have exactly one public folder format:
61	`artagents/orchestrators/<slug>/{orchestrator.yaml,SKILL.md,run.py}` for
62	orchestrators and `artagents/executors/<slug>/{executor.yaml,SKILL.md,run.py}`
63	for executors, with optional local `src/` modules. Top-level `artagents/*.py`
64	files are shared libraries or system commands, not alternate runnable
65	implementations.
66	
67	Before adding a new public capability, read `docs/creating-tools.md`. Create an
68	executor for one concrete unit of work, an orchestrator for a workflow, and an
69	element for a reusable render building block. Use
70	`docs/templates/executor/`, `docs/templates/orchestrator/`, or
71	`docs/templates/element/` as the starting shape.
72	
73	Do not chain pipeline internals by hand unless you are debugging one stage.
74	Source-analysis executors use files as their artifact contract; normal creative
75	requests should go through an orchestrator. If the user gives a topic instead
76	of a brief, use or create a brief-generation executor and coordinate it from an
77	orchestrator. Do not fake source media just to enter the source-video pipeline.
78	
79	Use canonical packages and commands for new code:
80	
81	```bash
82	python3 -m artagents orchestrators list
83	python3 -m artagents orchestrators inspect builtin.hype --json
84	python3 -m artagents orchestrators validate
85	python3 -m artagents orchestrators run builtin.hype --out runs/<name> --brief brief.txt --dry-run -- --target-duration 12 --from cut
86	python3 -m artagents orchestrators run builtin.event_talks --out runs/event --dry-run -- ados-sunday-template --out runs/event/talks.json
87	python3 -m artagents executors list
88	python3 -m artagents executors inspect builtin.render --json
89	python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.render --out runs/<name> --brief brief.txt --dry-run
90	python3 -m artagents executors inspect upload.youtube
91	python3 -m artagents executors run upload.youtube --dry-run --video-url https://cdn.example.com/talk.mp4 --title "Talk" --description "Description"
92	python3 -m artagents elements list
93	python3 -m artagents elements inspect effects text-card --json
94	python3 -m artagents elements fork effects text-card
95	```
96	
97	VibeComfy and Moirae are external executors only; do not expose them as orchestrators.
98	
99	`python3 -m artagents setup` is dry-run by default. Use `python3 -m artagents setup --apply` only when the user wants local managed element sync and local element dependency installation.
100	
101	Default orchestrators include `builtin.hype`, `builtin.event_talks`, `builtin.thumbnail_maker`, and `builtin.understand`. Default executors include the `STEP_ORDER` built-ins plus external executors such as `external.moirae` and `external.vibecomfy.run`. Default elements are bundled under `artagents/elements/bundled` and sync into `.artagents/elements/managed`; editable forks go under `.artagents/elements/overrides`.
102	
103	## Reigh Data Tool
104	
105	Use `artagents/executors/reigh_data/SKILL.md` before fetching live Reigh project, shot, task, timeline, image, or video data. The canonical command is:
106	
107	```bash
108	python3 -m artagents reigh-data --project-id <PROJECT_UUID> --shot-id <SHOT_UUID> --out runs/reigh/shot.json
109	```
110	
111	This calls the PAT-authenticated `reigh-data-fetch` Edge Function in `reigh-app`; do not add direct Supabase table queries in ArtAgents for this data.
112	
113	The main root launcher remains supported, and direct stage launchers live under `bin/`:
114	
115	```bash
116	python3 -m artagents --video SRC.mp4 --brief brief.txt --out runs/<name> --render
117	python3 bin/event_talks.py render --manifest runs/event/talks.json --out-dir runs/event/rendered
118	```
119	
120	For polished long event-talk videos, keep `bin/event_talks.py render` on its default `--renderer remotion-wrapper`: Remotion renders the animated intro/outro cards, while ffmpeg handles the long media pass, lower-third, corner logo, and final concat. Card renders are cached beside the card MP4s and are invalidated by talk metadata, dimensions, duration, and brand asset mtimes; use `--force-card-render` when iterating on card animation code. Full `--renderer remotion` writes Reigh-style timeline/assets JSON and renders the whole talk through `bin/render_remotion.py`, but it can be slow and disk-heavy for 10+ minute talks and now preflights free disk. `--renderer ffmpeg-proof` is only for quick boundary/proof checks, not final branded output.
121	
122	## Remotion Renderer
123	
124	Official Remotion agent skill: `remotion-best-practices`.
125	
126	```bash
127	npx skills add remotion-dev/skills
128	npx remotion skills add
129	```
130	
131	Use it for general Remotion background, but follow ArtAgents contracts first. The Remotion project is `remotion/`; normal ArtAgents renders go through `python3 bin/render_remotion.py`, not raw `npx remotion render`, because the wrapper builds props, resolves themes, serves assets with HTTP Range support, and avoids bundling large media.
132	
133	```bash
134	python3 bin/render_remotion.py \
135	  --timeline runs/<name>/briefs/<brief>/hype.timeline.json \
136	  --assets runs/<name>/briefs/<brief>/hype.assets.json \
137	  --out runs/<name>/briefs/<brief>/render.mp4
138	```
139	
140	```bash
141	cd remotion
142	npm run typecheck
143	npm run smoke
144	npm run gen-types
145	```
146	
147	Run `gen-types` after effect/theme element changes. For long event talks, prefer `bin/event_talks.py render --renderer remotion-wrapper`; use full `--renderer remotion` only when the whole talk must go through timeline/assets rendering.
148	
149	Guardrails: `TimelineComposition` lives in `remotion/src/Root.tsx`; use `calculateMetadata` for timeline/theme-derived duration, dimensions, fps, or props; keep props JSON-serializable; use explicit frame math and clamped `interpolate()` timing; consume registry URLs prepared by `bin/render_remotion.py`; preserve `_reference/README.md` semantics; do not put large media in `remotion/public/` or commit generated renders.
150	
151	## Generate Image Tool
152	
153	Use `bin/generate_image.py` for GPT Image API asset generation inside ArtAgents:
154	
155	```bash
156	python3 bin/generate_image.py \
157	  --prompt "A minimal editorial still of a red triangle on white" \
158	  --n 2 \
159	  --size 1024x1024 \
160	  --quality low \
161	  --output-format png \
162	  --out-dir runs/images \
163	  --manifest runs/images/manifest.json
164	```
165	
166	Prompt-list files are supported:
167	
168	- Plain text: one prompt per non-empty line.
169	- JSON array: `["prompt one", {"prompt": "prompt two", "n": 3, "size": "1536x1024"}]`
170	- JSONL: one string or object per line.
171	
172	Use `--dry-run` before expensive batches. API keys are read from the process environment, `this.env`, nearby workspace `.env` files, or an explicit `--env-file /path/to/.env`. Do not print or hardcode API keys.
173	
174	Current GPT Image defaults:
175	
176	- model: `gpt-image-2`
177	- size: `1024x1024`
178	- quality: `medium`
179	- output format: `png`
180	
181	`gpt-image-2` size rules: `WIDTHxHEIGHT` must use multiples of 16, max edge <= 3840, aspect ratio <= 3:1, and total pixels between 655,360 and 8,294,400.
182	
183	## Visual Understanding Tool
184	
185	Use `bin/visual_understand.py` when you need a cheap visual read on one image or a batch of sampled video frames. It can pass a single image directly, or build a numbered contact sheet from up to 20 images/frames before querying an OpenAI vision model.
186	
187	```bash
188	python3 bin/visual_understand.py \
189	  --video source.mp4 \
190	  --at 0,20,40,60,80,100,120,140 \
191	  --query "Which numbered frames are holding/title screens to remove, and which should be kept?" \
192	  --out runs/visual-understanding/review.json \
193	  --env-file /path/to/.env
194	```
195	
196	Defaults: `--mode fast` (`gpt-4o-mini`), `detail=low`, `cols=4`, `max-images=20`. Use fast first for normal review and boundary checks. If the answer is not detailed enough, the visual evidence is ambiguous, or the cut decision needs higher confidence, rerun with `--mode best` (`gpt-5.4`). Use `--model MODEL` only for explicit one-off overrides, `--compare-model MODEL` to compare additional models on the same contact sheet, and `--detail high` only for small text or dense visual evidence. Keep generated frames, contact sheets, and JSON answers under `runs/`.
197	
198	Use crop review when deciding vertical/social framing from one image or sampled frame:
199	
200	```bash
201	python3 bin/visual_understand.py \
202	  --video source.mp4 \
203	  --at 140 \
204	  --crop-aspect 9:16 \
205	  --crop-position left,center,right \
206	  --query "Which crop works best for 9:16 and keeps the speaker most readable?"
207	```
208	
209	`--crop-aspect` accepts repeated or comma-separated aspects such as `9:16,1:1`; `--crop-position` accepts alignments such as `left,center,right` or `top,center,bottom`. Crop review requires exactly one source image/frame and creates a numbered contact sheet of variants.
210	
211	If you do not know which frames to query, do not guess manually. Reuse or generate asset-level analysis first:
212	
213	```bash
214	python3 bin/scenes.py --video source.mp4 --out runs/event/scenes.json
215	python3 bin/shots.py --video source.mp4 --scenes runs/event/scenes.json --out runs/event/shots
216	python3 bin/event_talks.py find-holding-screens --video source.mp4 --out runs/event/holding-screens.json
217	python3 bin/boundary_candidates.py \
218	  --asset-key main \
219	  --video source.mp4 \
220	  --manifest runs/event/talks.json \
221	  --transcript runs/event/transcript/transcript.json \
222	  --scenes runs/event/scenes.json \
223	  --shots runs/event/shots/shots.json \
224	  --holding-screens runs/event/holding-screens.json \
225	  --out runs/event/boundary-candidates.json
226	```
227	
228	Store source-derived analysis at asset level. `hype.metadata.json` already uses `sources[asset_key].transcript_ref`, `scenes_ref`, `shots_ref`, and `quality_zones_ref`; boundary candidate packages should mirror that with `asset_key`, `asset_analysis`, and `metadata_source_refs`. Do not embed this analysis into `hype.timeline.json` or `hype.assets.json`; those stay Reigh-compatible and timelines only reference assets and edits.
229	
230	## Audio Understanding Tool
231	
232	Use `bin/audio_understand.py` when the edit question depends on how something sounds, not just what was said: emotional force, excitement, speed, pauses, laughter, applause, music/SFX, clipping, echo, room tone, or whether a quote has a clean in/out.
233	
234	Single source:
235	
236	```bash
237	python3 bin/audio_understand.py \
238	  --audio quote.wav \
239	  --query "Is this quote emotionally strong enough for an opener? Is the speaker too slow?" \
240	  --out runs/audio-understanding/quote-review.json \
241	  --env-file /path/to/.env
242	```
243	
244	Comparison sources:
245	
246	```bash
247	python3 bin/audio_understand.py \
248	  --audio quote-a.wav \
249	  --audio quote-b.wav \
250	  --audio quote-c.wav \
251	  --query "Which numbered quote sounds the most emotional and exciting? Rank them and flag any pacing problems." \
252	  --out runs/audio-understanding/quote-comparison.json
253	```
254	
255	For comparison, the tool builds a numbered audition reel: it says "Number 1", plays the first clip, says "Number 2", plays the second clip, and so on. This is the audio equivalent of a visual contact sheet: the model hears the candidates in one context and can compare delivery, pace, intensity, and production quality directly.
256	
257	For video, pass `--video source.mp4 --at 01:20,03:45 --window-sec 20` to extract windows around candidate moments. Multiple windows also default to a numbered audition reel. Use `--audition-reel never` when you want per-window independent analysis.
258	
259	Philosophical rule: transcript is factual text evidence; direct audio understanding is listening evidence. Use `bin/transcribe.py` for exact words and speaker timing, then use `bin/audio_understand.py` for embodied editorial judgment: urgency, hesitation, charm, tension, crowd response, music shape, and whether the cut feels alive.
260	
261	## Video Understanding Tool
262	
263	Use `bin/video_understand.py` when the edit question depends on synchronized picture and sound rather than frames alone or audio alone: gestures, speaker presence, camera movement, visual continuity, crowd reaction, music shape, production quality, and whether the moment lands as a complete video beat.
264	
265	```bash
266	python3 bin/video_understand.py \
267	  --video source.mp4 \
268	  --at 01:20,03:45 \
269	  --window-sec 20 \
270	  --query "Which moment works better as an opener? Consider picture, sound, energy, and clean in/out points." \
271	  --out runs/video-understanding/opener-review.json \
272	  --env-file /path/to/.env
273	```
274	
275	Defaults: `--mode fast` (`gemini-2.5-flash`) with extracted upload clips under `runs/video-understanding/video-windows`. Use `--mode best` (`gemini-2.5-pro`) when the synchronized evidence is subtle or high-stakes. If no `--at` or `--start/--end` is provided, the tool chunks the source into bounded windows. Keep generated clips and JSON answers under `runs/`.
276	
277	Use the unified `bin/understand.py` dispatcher when you want one entry point:
278	
279	```bash
280	python3 bin/understand.py image --image frame.jpg --query "What is happening here?"
281	python3 bin/understand.py audio --audio quote.wav
282	python3 bin/understand.py video --video source.mp4 --at 01:20
283	```
284	
285	Philosophical rule: visual understanding is frame/contact-sheet evidence, audio understanding is listening evidence, video understanding is synchronized sight-and-sound evidence, and transcript remains factual text evidence.
286	
287	## Sprite Sheet Setting
288	
289	Use `bin/sprite_sheet.py` when the user wants an animation asset, sprite sheet, chopped frames, or a preview video:
290	
291	```bash
292	python3 bin/sprite_sheet.py \
293	  --animation "8-frame idle bounce: squash down, stretch up, settle back to neutral" \
294	  --subject "small black five-point star mascot" \
295	  --cols 4 \
296	  --rows 2 \
297	  --frame-width 256 \
298	  --frame-height 256 \
299	  --fps 8 \
300	  --quality medium \
301	  --out-dir runs/sprites/star-idle \
302	  --env-file /path/to/.env
303	```
304	
305	The workflow:
306	
307	1. Compute exact sheet size from grid: `cols * frame_width` by `rows * frame_height`.
308	2. Generate `layout_guide.png`, an outline image that marks cell boundaries and safe areas.
309	3. Query GPT Image with technical sprite-sheet specs and the layout guide.
310	4. Save `sprite_sheet.png`.
311	5. Validate the returned PNG dimensions exactly match the planned sheet.
312	6. Slice cells into `frames/frame_001.png`, `frames/frame_002.png`, etc.
313	7. Optionally normalize/recenter frames and run AI upscaling on the transparent frame sequence.
314	8. Assemble `sprite_preview.mp4` for quick review and `sprite_preview_prores.mov` as a higher-quality animation master.
315	9. Write efficient web assets under `web/`: a WebP atlas, WebP frame sequence, web MP4 preview, and `sprite_web_manifest.json`.
316	10. Save `sprite_manifest.json` with prompt, layout, frame positions, outputs, FPS, and usage metadata.
317	
318	Use `--frames N` and let the tool auto-select rows/columns when possible. It chooses a compact valid sheet under `gpt-image-2` limits, preferring low wasted cells and near-square layouts. Default to `4x4` frames of `256x256` for a `1024x1024` sheet unless the user specifies otherwise. For short smoke tests, use `2x2` frames of `512x512` so the sheet is still `1024x1024` and valid for `gpt-image-2`.
319	
320	Prompt the animation as a precise sequence: pose count, motion arc, camera consistency, scale consistency, background, and any forbidden artifacts. The generated sheet should contain no text, labels, grid lines, frame separators, watermarks, or gutters.
321	
322	Transparent output defaults to chroma key for `gpt-image-2`: the prompt asks for a flat `--key-color` background, then ffmpeg removes that color into `sprite_sheet_alpha.png` and alpha PNG frames. Use `--no-transparent --background "..."` when a real background should remain. Native `background=transparent` works on transparent-capable GPT Image models such as `gpt-image-1.5`, but the sprite-sheet path uses chroma by default because it keeps the grid/dimension constraints deterministic.
323	
324	To remove/slice after generation without another API call:
325	
326	```bash
327	python3 bin/sprite_sheet.py \
328	  --input-sheet runs/sprites/star-idle/sprite_sheet.png \
329	  --animation "existing 30-frame run cycle" \
330	  --subject "same character" \
331	  --frames 30 \
332	  --frame-width 256 \
333	  --frame-height 256 \
334	  --fps 12 \
335	  --out-dir runs/sprites/star-idle-post
336	```
337	
338	If grid lines or key color leak into the generated sheet, rerun with a stricter prompt, adjust `--key-similarity` / `--key-blend`, use a different `--key-color`, or slice with `--slice-trim 4` to remove cell-edge artifacts.
339	
340	If characters drift out of frame after slicing, inspect `sprite_manifest.json` for `edge_warning_count`. Use `--normalize-frames --normalize-margin 18` to crop each frame to its alpha bounds, scale down only when necessary, and recenter it in the same frame size before building previews.
341	
342	For proper high-quality upscaling, upscale after transparency extraction and normalization, not before slicing and not from the final video. Use FAL Clarity Upscaler:
343	
344	```bash
345	python3 bin/sprite_sheet.py \
346	  --input-sheet runs/sprites/star-idle/sprite_sheet.png \
347	  --animation "existing 30-frame run cycle" \
348	  --subject "same character" \
349	  --frames 30 \
350	  --frame-width 512 \
351	  --frame-height 512 \
352	  --fps 12 \
353	  --normalize-frames \
354	  --ai-upscale-provider fal \
355	  --ai-upscale-factor 2 \
356	  --out-dir runs/sprites/star-idle-ai-upscaled \
357	  --force
358	```
359	
360	The FAL path uploads each transparent PNG frame to `fal-ai/clarity-upscaler`, downloads the enhanced result, then re-applies an upscaled copy of the original alpha mask so the background remains clean. Defaults are tuned for sprite preservation: low creativity and high resemblance. It reads `FAL_KEY` or `FAL_API_KEY` from the process, `--fal-env-file`, or nearby workspace `.env` files. Do not print or hardcode FAL keys.
361	
362	The local `--upscale-factor` path is only a deterministic ffmpeg fallback. Use it for fast previews, not final high-quality enlargement.
363	
364	For web delivery, prefer the default WebP atlas plus `sprite_web_manifest.json` for CSS/canvas playback, or individual WebP frames for lazy-loaded animation systems. When frames are normalized or upscaled, the tool rebuilds `sprite_sheet_processed.png` before web conversion so the atlas matches the final processed frame size. Use `--web-max-dim` to cap runtime frame size and `--web-quality` to tune file size. Animated WebP is opt-in with `--web-animated`; for 20-30 frame sprites it is usually less efficient and less controllable than atlas/canvas playback.
365	
366	## Important Contracts
367	
368	- `python3 -m artagents --brief ...` is the canonical top-level flow.
369	- Orchestrators coordinate executors and may call declared child orchestrators. Executors execute one unit and must not call orchestrators.
370	- `bin/cut.py` emits `hype.timeline.json`, `hype.assets.json`, `hype.metadata.json`, and `hype.edl.csv`.
371	- Reigh-facing JSON should round-trip through existing helpers and tests.
372	- Source-cut timelines preserve legacy `clipType="text"` overlays.
373	- Pure-generative timelines may use extended `clipType` values and `params`.
374	- Elements resolve in priority order: active theme, `.artagents/elements/overrides`, `.artagents/elements/managed`, then `artagents/elements/bundled`.
375	- After adding or renaming effects, animations, transitions, or theme elements, run:
376	
377	```bash
378	python3 scripts/gen_effect_registry.py
379	cd remotion
380	npm run gen-types
381	```
382	
383	## Validation
384	
385	Use focused tests for changed behavior:
386	
387	```bash
388	pytest tests/test_generate_image.py
389	pytest tests/test_schema_contract.py tests/test_pure_generative_pipeline.py
390	```
391	
392	For render-related changes, also run the relevant Remotion or render smoke tests already in `tests/`.

## Summary

Based on my investigation of the ArtAgents codebase, here are the answers to your two questions:

---

### 1. STREAMLINED HAPPY PATH FOR VIDEO TIMELINES

**The canonical one-shot command is:**
```bash
python3 -m artagents --brief BRIEF.txt --out runs/example [--video source.mp4] [--render]
```

**End-to-end workflow (numbers are steps from `STEP_ORDER` in pipeline.py):**

1. **Brief input** → Pipeline processes the brief
2. **Source analysis** (if `--video` present) → steps 1-8: transcribe, scenes, quality_zones, shots, triage, scene_describe, quote_scout, pool_build/merge
3. **Arrangement** (step 9) → LLM assembles clips from pool using brief
4. **Cut** (step 10) → Generates `hype.timeline.json` and `hype.assets.json`
5. **Refine** (step 11, optional) → Editor review refinement
6. **Render** (step 12, only if `--render` flag) → Invokes `bin/render_remotion.py` which reads timeline/assets and produces `hype.mp4`
7. **Validation** (step 13) → Optional validation

**Pure-generative path** (no source video):
```bash
python3 -m artagents --brief examples/briefs/cinematic.txt --out runs/example --target-duration 15 --render
```
Skips source analysis steps (1-8), jumps to arrangement using generative pools.

**Resume/skip capabilities:**
- `--from cut` forces cut and later to rerun
- `--skip refine` omits refine, goes straight cut→render
- `--render` flag is the control for whether render executes at all

---

### 2. TIMELINE CONTRACTS & RULES FOR AGENTS

**Root SKILL.md should include:**

1. **Top-level timeline fields agents must preserve** (from `_TIMELINE_TOP_ALLOWED`):
   - `theme` (required for Remotion renderability; may be absent in persisted Reigh timelines)
   - `theme_overrides` (optional; agent must preserve if present)

A real plan, sequenced by risk + dependency:

**Phase 0: Audit (one afternoon, doesn't change code).** Three greps tell you a lot:

- For each executor folder, who imports it / who runs it via `executors run`? (Find the dead ones.)

You can't sequence the rest until you know which of the abstractions are load-bearing vs nominal.

**Phase 1: Delete the duplicated surfaces.**

- `bin/` wrappers → delete the ones that are just thin shells; fold the ones doing real work into their executor's `run.py`. The spell already commits everyone to `python3 -m artagents`.
- Orchestrator registry → replace the hardcoded factory list with a folder scan over `artagents/orchestrators/*/orchestrator.yaml`. Adding a new builtin should be "drop a folder," nothing else.
- Recipe-as-orchestrator (`first_rite` and any siblings — the test is "wraps a single executor with a preset") → move to either named presets on the executor or a `recipes/` Python file.

After Phase 1 the codebase is meaningfully smaller and the per-tool SKILL.md docs are the *only* place tool details live.

**Phase 2: Make `Timeline` a real domain object.**

One class. Owns `load/dump` (unknown top-level fields preserved by construction). Owns `.for_render()` (defaults theme if absent). Holds `clips: list[Clip]` where `Clip` is a typed sum. Every executor that touches timelines goes through this class — direct `json.load` of `hype.timeline.json` becomes a lint failure.

This kills three of the rules I was about to put back in SKILL.md. Same pattern probably wants to apply to `Pool` / `AssetRegistry` but I'd defer that until after `Timeline` proves out.

**Phase 3: Collapse the parallel pipelines.**

Once clips dispatch on `kind`, "source-cut pipeline" and "pure-generative pipeline" stop being two things. `STEP_ORDER` becomes per-clip-kind capability discovery: the pipeline asks each clip what stages it needs, runs the union, dedupes. This is the highest-payoff, highest-risk piece — defer until Phase 2 lands and you have working tests.

**Phase 4: Reconsider the trinity (only if Phase 0 says it's nominal).**

If executors/orchestrators/elements are just three folder shapes with the same loader, collapse to one concept with a `kind:` field in the manifest. If the runtime actually treats them differently (different validation, different lifecycle), leave it — the spell sells the trinity well and it's not costing anything.

**What I wouldn't touch:**

- The CLI gateway (`python3 -m artagents`) — the "one gate" property is the best thing in the repo.
- The per-tool `SKILL.md` pattern — that's the right unit of documentation.
- The spell or the trimmed root SKILL.md.
- Reigh-app interop format. Round-tripping is the contract.

## D. Trinity reality check

**Verdict: STRUCTURAL.** Executors, orchestrators, and elements share a *folder-discovery + manifest-validation* idiom but have genuinely different schemas, runners, and lifecycles.

Evidence of distinct machinery:

| concern | executors | orchestrators | elements |
|---|---|---|---|
| schema | `executors/schema.py` (624 lines) — `ExecutorDefinition` with `inputs`, `outputs`, `command`, `isolation`, `cache`, `graph.depends_on` | `orchestrators/schema.py` (427 lines) — `OrchestratorDefinition` with `runtime`, `child_executors`, `child_orchestrators` | `elements/schema.py` (162 lines) — `ElementDefinition` with `kind`, `priority`, no command/runtime |
| folder loader | `executors/folder.py` (270 lines) | `orchestrators/folder.py` (248 lines) | none — `elements/registry.py:113–150` walks `bundled/` directly |
| runner | `executors/runner.py` (520 lines) — runs subprocess/built-in step | `orchestrators/runner.py` (480 lines) — different runtime kinds (`python` vs `command`) at lines 126–128, 233–242 | no runner — elements are render assets, not invoked |
| registry semantics | flat by id (`ExecutorRegistry`) | flat by id with cycle detection (`_validate_no_cycles` lines 131–151) and child-executor cross-validation (lines 105–113) | layered by `(kind, id)` with priority/source precedence (`ElementRegistry._all` lines 43–78) and conflict tracking (lines 66–78) |
| dispatch from `__main__` | `pipeline.py` → `executors run …` | `pipeline.py` → `orchestrators run …` | `pipeline.py` → `elements …` (install/list, no run) |

So they are not "three names for the same thing." They are three real contracts that happen to share a *folder-with-manifest* convention. The convention itself is generic (`_package_folder_roots`/`_package_manifest_paths` in both `executors/registry.py:189–218` and `orchestrators/registry.py:331–360` are duplicates) — that's a real refactor opportunity, but not a sign the trinity is fake.

+Default orchestrators include `builtin.hype`, `builtin.event_talks`, `builtin.thumbnail_maker`, and `builtin.understand`.

  "new_string": "def _builtin_folder_roots() -> tuple[Path, ...]:\n    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\n    skip = {\"__pycache__\", \"bundled\", \"curated\"}\n    return tuple(\n        path\n        for path in sorted(root.iterdir())\n        if path.is_dir() and path.name not in skip and (path / \"orchestrator.yaml\").is_file()\n    )"
}

1	from __future__ import annotations

3	from pathlib import Path
4	
5	PACKAGE_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
6	REPO_ROOT = PACKAGE_ROOT.parent
7	WORKSPACE_ROOT = REPO_ROOT.parent
8	
9	# Map of bin-style script filenames (e.g. "render_remotion.py") to the
10	# canonical executor module that owns the behavior. Keeps callers free to use
11	# the legacy filename while we migrate, and makes the one name mismatch
12	# (render_remotion -> executors.render) explicit in one place.
13	_EXECUTOR_MODULE_OVERRIDES = {
14	    "render_remotion": "artagents.executors.render.run",
15	}
16	
17	
18	def executor_argv(script_name: str, python_exec: str) -> list[str]:
19	    """Return argv tokens that invoke an executor's canonical module entrypoint.
20	
21	    `script_name` accepts either a bare step name (``"transcribe"``) or the
22	    legacy ``bin/`` filename (``"transcribe.py"``).
23	    """
24	    stem = script_name[:-3] if script_name.endswith(".py") else script_name
25	    module = _EXECUTOR_MODULE_OVERRIDES.get(stem, f"artagents.executors.{stem}.run")
26	    return [python_exec, "-m", module]

```
1	# ArtAgents Architecture
2	
3	ArtAgents has three canonical public concepts:
4	
5	- **Orchestrators** coordinate multi-step workflows.
6	- **Executors** run concrete work.
7	- **Elements** are render/custom building blocks such as effects, animations, and transitions.
8	
9	Canonical packages and commands are first-class. `python3 -m artagents` is the
10	executable package gateway for normal work. Retained `bin/*.py` launchers route
11	to canonical executor or orchestrator folders for specialized/manual use.
12	
13	## Onboarding Commands
14	
15	Run these from the repository root before editing:
16	
17	```bash
18	python3 -m artagents --help
19	git status --short
20	python3 -m artagents doctor
21	python3 -m artagents orchestrators list
22	python3 -m artagents executors list
23	python3 -m artagents elements list
24	python3 -m artagents setup
25	```
26	
27	`setup` is dry-run by default. `python3 -m artagents setup --apply` is the explicit local mutation path and delegates to element sync/install helpers.
28	
29	Canonical discovery commands are:
30	
31	```bash
32	python3 -m artagents orchestrators inspect builtin.hype --json
33	python3 -m artagents executors inspect builtin.render --json
34	python3 -m artagents elements inspect effects text-card --json
35	```
36	
37	These JSON commands are the runtime index for agents. Folder-backed
38	orchestrators and executors include metadata such as `orchestrator_root`,
39	`executor_root`, and `skill_file`; agents should load the ArtAgents entrypoint
40	skill first, then open only the specific folder-level skill needed for the
41	selected registry item. Do not package every executor and orchestrator skill
42	into one merged runtime prompt.
43	
44	Default orchestrators include `builtin.hype`, `builtin.event_talks`, `builtin.thumbnail_maker`, and `builtin.understand`. Default executors include every `STEP_ORDER` built-in, upload/action executors, Moirae, and VibeComfy. Default elements include bundled effects, animations, and transitions that can be synced into `.artagents/elements/managed` and forked into `.artagents/elements/overrides`.
45	
46	Each runnable orchestrator has exactly one canonical implementation location:
47	`artagents/orchestrators/<slug>/{orchestrator.yaml,SKILL.md,run.py}` with
48	optional local `src/` modules. Each runnable executor has exactly one canonical
49	implementation location:
50	`artagents/executors/<slug>/{executor.yaml,SKILL.md,run.py}` with optional local
51	`src/` modules. Top-level `artagents/*.py` modules are shared libraries or
52	system commands only; they are not alternate executor or orchestrator
53	implementations.
54	
55	For creation decisions, use `docs/creating-tools.md` and the templates under
56	`docs/templates/`. Add an executor for one concrete action, an orchestrator for
57	a workflow, and an element for a reusable render primitive. Agents should avoid
58	manual chains of low-level stage artifacts unless they are debugging a specific
59	executor.
60	
61	## Orchestrators
62	
63	| Module or entry point | Classification | Notes |
64	| --- | --- | --- |
65	| `python3 -m artagents`, `artagents/__main__.py` | System entry point | Executable package gateway for all canonical commands. |
66	| `artagents/pipeline.py` | System command and dispatcher | Cache-aware hype command support and source of `STEP_ORDER`; not a second orchestrator format. |
67	| `artagents/orchestrators/hype` | Orchestrator | Canonical built-in hype orchestrator folder. |
68	| `artagents/orchestrators/event_talks` | Orchestrator | Canonical event-talk discovery and rendering workflow folder. |
69	| `artagents/orchestrators/thumbnail_maker` | Orchestrator | Canonical source-evidence thumbnail workflow folder. |
70	| `artagents/orchestrators/understand` | Orchestrator | Canonical dispatcher for audio, visual, and video understanding executors. |
71	| `bin/event_talks.py`, `bin/thumbnail_maker.py`, `bin/understand.py` | Launchers | Thin direct launchers backed by canonical orchestrator folders. |
72	| `artagents/orchestrators/*` | Orchestrator canonical package | Folderized orchestrator manifests, registry, runner, and CLI. |
73	
74	## Executors
75	
76	Every runnable tool is a built-in or external executor exposed from exactly one canonical folder under `artagents/executors/<slug>/`. Retained `bin/*.py` launchers import canonical executor folder entrypoints and do not own behavior.
77	
78	| Executor group | Canonical location | Retained launchers | Notes |
79	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
80	| Hype pipeline stages | `artagents/executors/{transcribe,scenes,quality_zones,shots,triage,scene_describe,quote_scout,pool_build,pool_merge,arrange,cut,refine,render,editor_review,validate}` | Matching `bin/*.py` launchers | `STEP_ORDER` stages used by the hype orchestrator. |
81	| Understanding tools | `artagents/executors/{audio_understand,visual_understand,video_understand}` | Matching `bin/*.py` launchers | Concrete media understanding tools used directly or by the understand orchestrator. |
82	| Standalone/service tools | `artagents/executors/{asset_cache,boundary_candidates,generate_image,human_notes,inspect_cut,open_in_reigh,publish,reigh_data,sprite_sheet,upload_youtube}` | Matching `bin/*.py` launchers where useful | Standalone executor capabilities. |
83	| External tools | `artagents/executors/{vibecomfy,moirae}` | None required | VibeComfy and Moirae are external executors only, not orchestrators. |
84	
85	Executor-owned complexity stays in the executor folder, usually under optional local `src/` modules. Shared pure hype/editing logic belongs in `artagents/domains/hype`; generic plumbing belongs in `artagents/utilities`.
86	
87	## Element Support
88	
89	| Module or path | Classification | Notes |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
```

# ArtAgents ↔ Reigh Timeline Compatibility Report

## 1. Reigh's timeline data shape

The canonical persisted shape is the Zod schema at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts` (the `@banodoco/timeline-schema` package — Reigh consumes it; ArtAgents' `artagents/timeline.py:21-30` re-exports the Python twin). Reigh's editor types live at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts:226-238` (`TimelineConfig`) and re-export the shared types as `SharedTimelineConfig` etc.

- **Produced** by: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/serialize.ts` (`serializeForDisk`, `validateSerializedConfig`); created blank by `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/defaults.ts:24-42`.
- **Consumed/rendered** by `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/TimelineRenderer.tsx` and `/.../components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.test.tsx`.
- **Persisted** in Postgres `public.timelines.config jsonb` (and `asset_registry jsonb`), defined at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/supabase/migrations/20260325090000_create_video_editor_tables.sql:6-7`. Versioned writes via `update_timeline_config_versioned` (`.../20260326100000_*.sql`). Imports go through edge function `/.../supabase/functions/timeline-import/handler.ts:68` which Zod-parses with `TimelineConfig`.

## 2. Field-by-field comparison

ArtAgents `examples/hype.timeline.full.json` and the schema declare the same top-level set: `theme`, `theme_overrides`, `tracks`, `clips`, `pinnedShotGroups`, `generation_defaults`, `output`. ArtAgents' Python allowlist at `artagents/timeline.py:345` is exactly `{theme, theme_overrides, generation_defaults, clips, tracks, pinnedShotGroups, output}` — matches Reigh's `ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` at `serialize.ts:109-117` exactly.

Clip fields are also aligned: Reigh's `TIMELINE_CLIP_FIELDS` (`serialize.ts:8-42`) is byte-equivalent to ArtAgents' `_CLIP_ALLOWED` (`timeline.py:347-355`). Both include the Sprint-2 schema-lift fields: `params`, `pool_id`, `clip_order`, `source_uuid`, `generation`. Track fields (`_TRACK_ALLOWED`, `timeline.py:356`) match `TRACK_DEFINITION_FIELDS` (`serialize.ts:46-56`).

**Asymmetries / dropped fields:**
- `output.background` and `output.background_scale` are emitted by Reigh as `null` (`defaults.ts:36-37`), but the shared Zod `TimelineOutput` declares them as `optional` (no `.nullable()`) at `schemas.ts:119-125`. A literal `null` from Reigh will fail `TimelineConfigSchema.safeParse` in `timeline-import/handler.ts:68` — and the Python `_TIMELINE_OUTPUT` shape doesn't model `null` either. This is a pre-existing bug, not something the refactor introduces.
- ArtAgents allows `output.file` to be omitted at the timeline level (it materialises one via `materialize_output` `timeline.py:106-111`); Reigh always writes it.
- The brief mentions a source `codec` pass-through (`CARRY_FORWARD_SOURCE_FIELDS` `timeline.py:377`) — that lives on **pool entries**, not on the timeline. It's not part of the round-trip with Reigh and is irrelevant to Phase 2.

## 3. Theme handling on the Reigh side

Reigh **routinely persists timelines without a theme**: `defaults.ts:24-42` explicitly leaves `theme`/`theme_overrides`/`generation_defaults` undefined for new editor sessions. The shared schema says `theme: z.string().optional()` (`schemas.ts:143`).

Reigh's render path **does not require** `theme` on the timeline itself: `renderRouter.ts:194-199` defines a `FALLBACK_THEME_ID = '2rp'` and applies it when `config.theme` is missing or non-string. Crucially, Reigh nowhere treats `theme === null` as a sentinel — only `undefined`/missing or a non-empty string. There is no `theme: null` written anywhere I could find.

By contrast, ArtAgents' `validate_timeline` at `timeline.py:861-862` raises `Timeline.theme must be a non-empty slug` — this is the ArtAgents-only render-side requirement the safety plan calls out.

**Verdict on `.for_render()` injecting a default theme:** **safe**, provided ArtAgents (a) injects only at the render boundary (does not write the default back to disk), and (b) does not also alter `theme_overrides`. Reigh assumes `theme=undefined` → "use renderer default", so an ArtAgents-side `.for_render()` that picks `banodoco-default` (or whatever the catalog default is) is symmetric to Reigh's `'2rp'` fallback. No "null means something specific" semantics exist.

## 4. Clip-kind compatibility

Reigh's clip type is **a single open `string`** at the schema layer (`schemas.ts:60`, `types/index.ts:67-69`), with `BUILTIN_CLIP_TYPES = ['media', 'hold', 'text', 'effect-layer']`. There is **no** `clip.kind` field — only `clip.clipType`. Reigh has no concept of "source-cut vs pure-generative" pipelines: that distinction is Banodoco-side only (see `is_all_generative_arrangement` `timeline.py:1056` and `artagents/domains/hype/enriched_arrangement.py`).

What Reigh actually emits in clips:
- `clipType: 'media'` for everything backed by `asset` (videos and images both — distinguished by `assetEntry.type` MIME, not clipType). See `compositions/VisualClip.tsx:171-189`, `lib/editor-utils.ts:198`.
- `clipType: 'hold'` for background-fill clips (`migrate.ts:158`).
- `clipType: 'text'` with a `text` blob (`types/index.ts:110-118`).
- `clipType: 'effect-layer'` for generated Remotion modules (`TimelineRenderer.tsx:179`, `compositions/VisualClip.tsx:316`).
- Arbitrary theme-effect ids — anything in the registry. ArtAgents' fixture includes `clipType: 'text-card'`.

**Risk for the proposed typed sum `VideoSegmentClip | GenerativeImageClip | …`:**
- Reigh does not split video vs image at the clipType axis. A naive mapping that picks `VideoSegmentClip` based on `clipType === 'media' && asset is video` requires resolving `assetEntry.type` from the **asset registry**, not the timeline alone. The timeline by itself is ambiguous.
- `clipType: 'effect-layer'` and arbitrary theme-scoped strings (`text-card`, plus anything Sprint-5 effect registry adds) cannot be exhaustively typed. The sum needs an open `OtherClip` / `EffectLayerClip` arm or it will reject Reigh-produced timelines.
- Per-track-kind dispatch (visual vs audio) is in Reigh on `track.kind`, not clip.kind — `useAssetManagement.ts:217`, `editor-utils.ts:198`. Any "kind" added to clips would be redundant with this.

A Reigh-produced timeline survives only if dispatch defaults unknown `clipType` to a passthrough arm and never narrows on `clip.kind` (there is no such field). The plan to "dispatch on `clip.kind`" needs adjustment: Reigh has no `kind` and adding one would break the round-trip unless ArtAgents also strips it before save.

## 5. Risks & recommendations

- **Don't add `clip.kind` as a persisted field.** It's not in `_CLIP_ALLOWED` (`timeline.py:347-355`) or `TIMELINE_CLIP_FIELDS` (`serialize.ts:8-42`), and Reigh's `validateSerializedConfig` (`serialize.ts:119-141`) **throws** on unknown clip keys (closed allowlist). Treat `kind` as a runtime-derived view inside the `Timeline` class only, computed from `clipType` + asset MIME. If ArtAgents must persist a kind, add it to the shared schema package first and bump `@banodoco/timeline-schema` in lockstep.
- **`theme_overrides`/`generation_defaults` preservation must round-trip byte-equivalent.** Both sides already use closed top-level allowlists in lockstep; the new `Timeline` class must not add or normalise inner keys. The safety plan explicitly demands byte-equivalence (`docs/reigh-artagents-timeline-safety-plan.md:190,197`).
- **`.for_render()` default-theme injection is safe** but should never be written back to disk. Reigh persists `theme=undefined` and relies on its own `'2rp'` fallback (`renderRouter.ts:194-199`); if ArtAgents writes `theme: 'banodoco-default'` into a re-saved timeline, Reigh users would silently see a theme switch.
- **Typed clip sum needs an open arm.** `clipType` is open string by design (SD-024 comment at `types/index.ts:62-69`, `schemas.ts:54`). The sum must include `OpaqueClip { clipType: string; … }` for unknown types, mirroring Reigh's loud-placeholder fallback (`compositions/VisualClip.tsx:171`). Otherwise pure-Reigh timelines using future theme effects will round-trip-fail in ArtAgents.
- **Pre-existing `null` bug worth flagging now**: `defaults.ts:36-37` emits `background: null` / `background_scale: null`; the shared Zod (`schemas.ts:119-125`) and ArtAgents output type don't accept `null`. Any new `Timeline.from_dict` strictness will trip on Reigh-default rows. Fix in `@banodoco/timeline-schema` (use `.nullable()`) before tightening ArtAgents.
- **Schema location:** the `Timeline` *behaviour* (round-trip preserve, `.for_render()`, dispatch helpers) belongs in ArtAgents — Reigh has its own renderer and doesn't want a Python class. The *shape* must stay in `@banodoco/timeline-schema` (already shared by both repos: TS source at `node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts`, Python at the same package's `python/banodoco_timeline_schema/`). ArtAgents should validate against that schema (it already does — `timeline.py:30,858` calls `_shared_validate_timeline`); no change needed.
- **Round-trip already partly under-tested:** the safety plan flags that low-level serializer tests pass while real save flows may drop fields (`docs/reigh-artagents-timeline-safety-plan.md:354`). Reigh has unit tests at `lib/serialize.test.ts` and `lib/timeline-save-utils.test.ts`, but no end-to-end test asserting an ArtAgents-written file → `timeline-import` → DB → Reigh load → re-export is byte-equivalent. Phase 2 should add one fixture per top-level field combination before changing `clipType` dispatch.
